conviction_note: Q3 revenue is pre-released and the print turns on the Q4 guide (bar ~+10% q/q, GM 66-68%) and 2027 commentary; counterparties that spoke after TSMC (ASML 10-14, Broadcom 10-12) point to demand at or above that bar, and the ADR enters ~10% off its 10-05 record on sector/macro selling. Against that, the name sold its last beat-and-raise (-3.8% in July on a GM guide-down), and call-bid skew (-8.4) already pays for upside, so p_up is only 55. Findings sum +1.1 against a scaled +0.45; the gap is that several small positives each carry their own weight, while the scaled number puts the reaction-function risk into p_up.
bar: Q4 2026 revenue guide vs ~+10% q/q on Q3 (~US$47bn): Economic Daily News base case +10% q/q and GM guide 66-68% (https://money.udn.com/money/story/5607/9805612, 2026-10-10); Morgan Stanley +10-15% q/q (https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/tsmc-earnings-q3-2026-preview, 2026-10-12); KGI high-single-digit q/q, Q4 GM 67.6% (https://finance.technews.tw/2026/10/02/kgi-gives-tsmc-a-target-price-of-nt3200/, 2026-10-02). Q3 GM bar disputed: Hudson Labs consensus 66.5% (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/tsmc-q3-2026-earnings-preview-tsm-revenue-and-margins, 2026-09-28) vs MS 67.5% and KGI 68%. EPS consensus ~US$4.40/ADR (US$0.88/share, Hudson Labs). print_vs_bar_pct is my estimate of the Q4 revenue guide midpoint vs the +10% q/q bar.
positioning_check: Short interest 30.49m ADR shares at 2026-09-30 settlement, ~0.6% of shares, 3.06 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/tsm/short-interest, per sweep row read 2026-10-14). Not crowded. Baseline 25d skew -8.41 vol points (calls bid, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 1.37, event-implied move 3.59% (straddle 3.95% to 10-16 expiry); Admiral Markets cites +/-4.3% implied and a 10-year average move of +/-4.9%. Run-in: -7.29% over 5 days, -9.9% from 52w high; ADR record close US$485.80 on 10-05, US$453.31 on 10-09, spot 437.78 at seal.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue was NT$1,494.2bn (sum of monthly reports, Sept NT$511.9bn); with the TWD at 31.5-31.9 through September and flat over the quarter (31.852 at 9-30), that is roughly US$47.0-47.4bn against a US$44.6-45.8bn guide and a US$45.8bn Hudson Labs consensus dated 9-28, i.e. ~3% above the top of the range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 also beat the top of revenue guidance and EPS by ~13%; the ADR fell ~3.8% (Admiral Markets; pre-market ~$402 from $419.48, INDmoney). Revenue is pre-released monthly, so the line rarely moves the stock on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced in NT$ terms; the stale US$45.8bn consensus (Hudson, 9-28) has not visibly moved to ~US$47bn in the previews, but every desk can do the division. If it were not priced the previews would not all say 'above guidance'.
findings.independence: TWD rates from https://udn.com/news/story/7239/9786115 (2026-09-30, Q3 TWD -0.05%, 9-30 close 31.852); same monthly-revenue document as the margin finding below.

findings.finding: Q3 gross margin likely lands at 67-68%, above the 65-67% guide and the 66.5% Hudson consensus: TSMC beat the top of its GM guide in Q1 2026 (66.2% vs 63-65%) and Q2 2026 (67.7% vs 65.5-67.5%), and Q3 revenue ran ~3% above the top of the guide. Offset: the guide assumed NT$32/US$ and the TWD averaged nearer 31.6, about -0.4pt at TSMC's 0.4pt-per-1% sensitivity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 GM 67.7% beat the top of the range and the stock still fell ~3.8% on a lower Q3 GM guide; Q1 2026 GM beat by >1pt (reaction not reliably sourced; one low-quality mirror says -3.1%).
findings.source_date: 2026-01-15 (Q1 guide 63-65% at NT$31.6); Q1 actual 66.2% from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1046179/000104617926000199/a1q26e_withguidancexfinal.htm (2026-04-16)
findings.why_not_priced: The published consensus (66.5%) sits below the pattern, but the sell-side whispers are already higher (MS 67.5%, KGI 68%), so only the gap between 66.5 and ~67.5 is open, and the bar is disputed.
findings.independence: KGI 68% (https://finance.technews.tw/2026/10/02/kgi-gives-tsmc-a-target-price-of-nt3200/); FX from https://udn.com/news/story/7239/9786115. Shares the Q3 revenue document with the finding above.

findings.finding: Counterparties that spoke after TSMC's July call point to a Q4 guide at or above the ~+10% q/q bar: ASML (10-14) guided Q4 sales to EUR14.2-15.2bn vs EUR11.7bn in Q3, said customers are raising short- and medium-term equipment forecasts and that planned 2027-28 supply 'will not fully meet' demand, and named TSMC leading a larger-reticle consortium and committing to High-NA HVM ~2030; Broadcom's CEO (10-12) kept FY27 AI semiconductor revenue at $115bn and said compute demand stays robust to 2030.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: January 2026: capex and outlook well above consensus and the stock jumped (Motley Fool via Yahoo); July 2026: FY growth raised to >40% and Q3 revenue guide ~$2bn above consensus, but a lower GM guide and the stock fell ~3.8%. Guidance is the line this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: ASML's release came out the morning of the seal and its own shares traded lower (Investing.com: -1.86% close, -2.26% after hours) because ASML held its Q4/FY range, so the read-through to TSMC's own guide has not been bid; the ADR is still ~10% off its 10-05 record after Hock Tan's 'casino' remark and the OpenAI revenue report. If priced, TSM would have recovered toward $450-485 with the Broadcom reaffirmation.
findings.independence: Broadcom: https://cryptobriefing.com/broadcom-hock-tan-ai-investors-gamblers/ (2026-10-12). ASML call detail: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-asml-tops-q3-2026-estimates-but-shares-fall-93CH-4948118. These are counterparty statements, not TSMC's own guide.

findings.finding: 2027 wafer price increases: DIGITIMES (9-24) reports supply-chain sources saying wafer-out prices are 'confirmed' up ~3-6% from January 2027, advanced nodes higher, with order visibility to 2030; Nikkei/KGI put advanced nodes at +5-10% and advanced packaging at +10-15%. TSMC has not confirmed; the call is where 2027 margin and pricing commentary comes out.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced reaction to a pricing comment on a call. C.C. Wei has said TSMC will not raise prices in short bursts like memory (udn, July).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the reports have been public since July (Nikkei) and September. What is open is confirmation; management usually declines to quantify, so the most likely outcome is little new.
findings.independence: KGI note https://finance.technews.tw/2026/10/02/kgi-gives-tsmc-a-target-price-of-nt3200/ (2026-10-02). Different source, same rumour chain.

findings.finding: The ADR enters the print -7.3% over 5 days and ~10% below its US$485.80 record close of 10-05 on sector and macro drivers that are not TSMC-specific: an OpenAI annualised-revenue report ~US$20bn below earlier figures, the US 10-year near 5.23% (10-08), Hock Tan's 'casino' remark (10-12), the CXMT memory headline and KOSPI -5.5% (10-13), and >NT$100bn of foreign selling in Taipei on 10-13 with TSMC -~2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026 the stock had run into the print and fell on a beat; this time it has de-rated into it. No sourced precedent for a de-rated entry.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown itself is the price; the claim is that it is sector-wide AI-funding fear that a reassuring call can reverse. But the 25d skew is -8.4 (calls already bid), so the options market already pays for the rebound; only part of it is open.

findings.finding: Margin dilution risk on the Q4 GM guide: CFO said the 2nm ramp dilutes H2 gross margin by 3-4pt and overseas fabs by 2-3pt early, rising to 3-4pt later; with N2 share rising in Q4 a GM guide at or below the 66% low end of the EDN base case is possible. The July reaction (-3.8%) was on exactly this line, a GM guide-down despite a beat and raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: Q3 GM guide midpoint 66% vs 67.7% in Q2, stock -3.8% (Admiral Markets) with record results.
findings.why_not_priced: Known dilution, but consensus Q4 GM (KGI 67.6%, EDN 66-68%) assumes it is offset by pricing and cost gains; a guide below 66% is not in those numbers. Short interest is 0.6% (not crowded), so no squeeze argument shrinks this negative.
findings.independence: Dilution figures repeated in https://www.digitimes.com.tw/tech/dt/n/shwnws.asp?id=769567 (2026-09-24); same management statement, counted once.

findings.finding: Capex: KGI expects 2027 capex of US$70-72bn vs US$60-64bn for 2026, and ASML says TSMC committed to High-NA HVM ~2030; an initial 2027 capex signal above ~US$70bn is possible on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: January 2026 capex $52-56bn vs ~$41-50bn expected and the stock jumped; July 2026 raise to $60-64bn and shares fell about 2% that morning (TrendForce/search summary). Mixed sign.
findings.why_not_priced: TSMC normally gives the next year's capex in January, so October commentary is usually qualitative; the sign of a capex surprise has been inconsistent for this name.

October 2026 monthly revenue: not released until ~2026-11-10, outside the window
Section 232 semiconductor tariffs: no October 2026 action found; latest is Taiwan saying there is no US timetable and preferential terms are agreed (May 2026)
Precise ADR close-to-close reactions for the January and April 2026 prints: not reliably sourced
TSMC-specific negative news in the 5-day drawdown: none found; drivers were sector/macro

baseline_tension: The evidence leans positive, which agrees with the call-bid skew (-8.4) and cuts against the 5-day run-down (-7.3%). The skew means part of the rebound is already paid for, and the July beat-and-raise sold off, so p_up sits at 55, not higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold its July beat-and-raise): Q3 revenue finding 0.2 -> 0.1, Q3 GM finding 0.5 -> 0.3

Lesson 6 (bar disputed for Q3 GM: 66.5 Hudson vs 67.5 MS vs 68 KGI): GM finding kept small; Q4 revenue bar has three roughly agreeing sources (~+10% q/q), so guidance findings not capped further; print_vs_bar 1.0 -> 0.5
Lesson 5 (counterparty/proxy evidence, not TSMC's own number): Q4 guide read-through 0.7 -> 0.6; price-hike rumour 0.3 -> 0.2; capex 0.2 -> 0.1
Lesson 7 (skew already pays for upside, -8.4 calls bid): positioning finding 0.6 -> 0.4; p_up 56 -> 55
Lesson 7 short-interest check done before the negative margin finding: 0.6% SI, 3.06 DTC, not crowded, so -0.6 stands
Untrustworthy-history lesson: base rate rebuilt from the option-implied move and Admiral's 10-year +/-4.9% average; abs_move_pct 4.5 unchanged
